newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Bonos closed little higher after dull day on Tuesday, with prices moving positively but without any domestic driving factors, dealers said.

"It was the same as yesterday apart from the fact prices were going in the opposite direction," a dealer at Bank of America in Madrid said. He added the market was still looking for direction, and on Wednesday it was likely to focus on U.S. September CPI. Forecasters put it at 3.1 percent from 2.9.
"For tomorrow it is likely we will see a weak start, in line with the selling we had at the close today," he added. On the Meff, the December contract support will be 107.40, then 107.00.
On the cash market the 10-year benchmark rose to 107.13 from 106.95, yielding 7.69 percent, while the 10-year spread over German Bunds was little wider at 171 from 170.
On the shorter part of the curve dealers expect a possible rise in yields in the coming days.
"Today we saw people selling on the high side, especially from outside," a dealer said. The February 2001 bond rose to 111.81 from 111.67 on Monday, with the yield of 6.84.
